issue_context.title: Reachable assert in ECDiffieHellmanCng
comments:
The assert was introduced with #72120, but the relevant code path there previously triggered an exception (verified by running against an older runtime on my machine), which is also not good, because `.GetECDiffieHellmanPrivateKey()` is documented as returning null, not throwing.

I'm no CNG expert, but from what I can tell the Debug.Assert there is correct.

My understanding is CNG has the unfortunate limitation that keys originally created as ECDSA keys cannot be used for ECDH, but keys created as ECDH can be used for either ECDSA or ECDH.

So my understanding is that the only way for unit test in the top post to work on Windows while backed by CNG is if:
a) `ECDsa.Create` were changed to create the key as an ECDH private key such that CNG allows it to work with ECDH and ECDS, or
b) `.GetECDiffieHellmanPrivateKey()` were enhanced to detect if the private key is ECDSA but is readable, and if so, read the key, and re-create it as ECDH. 

I'm not actually sure if either are desirable or not.

If neither such change is made, then IMHO, the correct behavior would be:
1. `loaded.loaded.HasPrivateKey = true`
1. `loaded.GetECDiffieHellmanPublicKey()` works because the cert allows all key usages by not constraining them.
1. `loaded.GetECDiffieHellmanPrivateKey()` returns null, because no private key that is usable for ECDH is currently available.
1. both `GetECDsa(Public|Private)Key` extension methods work.

> ) ECDsa.Create were changed to create the key as an ECDH private key such that CNG allows it to work with ECDH and ECDS, or

This is not a full fix, because the actual problem from the example is that the PKCS12 has a bag attribute saying "I am ECDSA, so my private key material should be imported in to CNG as ECDSA". So if we ever get a PKCS12/PFX with one of those bag attributes, the problem remains.

> .GetECDiffieHellmanPrivateKey() were enhanced to detect if the private key is ECDSA but is readable, and if so, read the key, and re-create it as ECDH.

That is... possible, but CNG gets a little iffy about exporting private keys that were imported from a PFX. They would need to be "encrypted" exports, and we would need to tear apart the PKCS#8 manually because the PKCS#8 blob _also_ preserves the key algorithm, so we would just end up round-tripping back to the same problem. This also wouldn't work if the key were totally non-exportable (either by policy or by provider limitation).

The last option you outlined is probably "right" to me, in spirit with CNG. If someone really wanted to, I suppose they could call `GetECDsaPrivateKey`, export the parameters if they are exportable, and import them back in as ECDiffieHellman.

review_comments:
Null works.  I slightly wonder if an exception would be more appropriate.  Because we have the problem of

* cert.HasPrivateKey: true
* cert.GetECDiffieHellmanPublicKey: non-null (not restricted by KU)
* cert.GetECDiffieHellmanPrivateKey: ???

For everything else, I believe that `(true, non-null)` => non-null (or perhaps an exception)... but I guess it does match the docs "or null if this certificate does not have an ECDiffieHellman private key.".... the private key happens to be ECDSA.

So, yeah.  I'm on the fence and waffling.

An exception is what we are doing today (once you get past the assert). The exception is not half-bad, either:

> Keys used with the ECDiffieHellmanCng algorithm must have an algorithm group of ECDiffieHellman.

`null` makes more sense to me since that is what the docs say it will do. CNG has some notion of "Hey your key is ECDSA" and returning null from these methods is what we do for the wrong algorithm. It is only a... little... odd that the public key fetch happens to work because the public half is not constrained.

Yeah. We definitely shouldn't crack the key to ask if it's ECDSA before returning the ECDH, since `new X509Certificate2(cert.RawData).GetECDiffieHellmanPublicKey()` wouldn't know to then return null.

So.  Yeah.  OK.  Let's go with null.  ECDH isn't super popular (from a cert) so it... hopefully... doesn't trip anyone up too badly.
